done_state: tessera/gitops/ manages dev/integration/FT/prod stage repos on the operator's separate-repo-per-stage convention: promotion, tag-checkpointed rollback that never touches store's ticket data, on-read ancestry reconciliation (stale, un-flagged when restored, never latched), and a diff() call for api's discrepancy computation -- with a promote-break-rollback-assert cycle demonstrated end to end.

criteria.statement: init_stage() creates a stage as its own independent git repository (not a git-worktree-linked checkout), matching the operator's confirmed convention.
init_stage() and promote_stage() refuse to operate on a stage repo path under an iCloud Drive / Dropbox / other sync-client-managed folder, per SCOPE.md premortem item 11.

promote_stage(stage, commit_sha, actor) fast-forwards the stage repo to commit_sha, tags a checkpoint at the new HEAD, and records a StagePromoted event via store (never writing stage_heads directly).
promote_stage() raises a clear error (does not silently no-op or force) when the target commit is not a fast-forward from the stage repo's current HEAD.
rollback_stage(stage, target_tag, actor) resets the stage repo's HEAD to a prior tagged checkpoint, records a StageRolledBack event via store, and never modifies any ticket data in store.

reconcile_stage(stage) flags a linked ticket stale when its linked commit is no longer an ancestor of the stage's real current HEAD (via git merge-base --is-ancestor), regardless of whether the HEAD move went through gitops or was a direct git operation on the stage repo.

reconcile_stage(stage) un-flags a previously-stale ticket the moment its linked commit is an ancestor of HEAD again (e.g. after re-promotion) -- staleness is recomputed from ancestry, never a one-way latch.

A full promote -> break (direct git reset bypassing gitops) -> rollback -> assert cycle is demonstrated end to end: code is reverted in the stage repo AND every ticket linked to the broken commit shows the stale flag, matching SCOPE.md's required evidence bar.
criteria.verification: python3 tests/test_promotion_cycle.py exits 0 and reports code_reverted=true tickets_flagged_stale=true.

criteria.statement: diff(stage, commit_sha) returns the real git diff/show output for that commit in that stage's repo, usable by api for discrepancy computation against a claim's files_touched.

Ticket-to-commit links (via store.link_ticket_commit) record a commit SHA; a branch name may additionally be recorded as informational only and is never used by reconcile_stage()'s ancestry check (SCOPE.md distinguishes the two).

failure_criteria.statement: promote_stage force-pushes/force-resets past a non-fast-forward instead of raising.
failure_criteria.detection: C4 explicitly tests the rejection path.

failure_criteria.statement: A promotion/rollback numeric or behavioral claim in a comment has no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the diff for numeric claims; each must name the command that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: Code assumes a stage repo directory exists without checking/creating it.
failure_criteria.detection: init_stage() is idempotent and required before any promote/rollback call touches a stage.

failure_criteria.statement: A git subprocess failure is swallowed (return code checked but not surfaced).
failure_criteria.detection: Every subprocess.run call in gitops uses check=True or explicitly inspects returncode and raises with the captured stderr.

failure_criteria.statement: reconcile_stage() only fires when gitops itself performs a promotion/rollback, missing a direct git operation on the stage repo (the exact hole ARCHITECTURE.md's revision fixed).
failure_criteria.detection: C6 explicitly tests a direct 'git reset' bypassing gitops entirely.

out_of_scope: Merge-conflict resolution (promote_stage requires a clean fast-forward; anything else is the operator's job via normal git).
Managing the source repo that stages promote FROM -- gitops operates only on the stage repos themselves.
constraints: Python 3.9+ stdlib only (subprocess, pathlib) plus tessera.common and tessera.store.
Uses the operator's confirmed convention: separate independent git repo per stage, ordered commits + tags -- never git worktree.
Every stage_heads write goes through store's StagePromoted/StageRolledBack events, never a direct store.stage_heads write.
